tier: Cross-cutting · every term an interviewer might drop into conversation expecting an instant, correct one-liner back

cards.back: Open standard letting independent agents built on different frameworks discover each other, delegate tasks, and collaborate. Complements MCP (which connects an agent to its tools) rather than replacing it.
RAG where an agent decides whether/how/when to retrieve, potentially iterating or reformulating queries, rather than a fixed retrieve-then-generate pipeline.

cards.front: What does RAGAS's Answer Relevancy metric measure?
cards.back: Whether an answer actually addresses the question asked, computed via embedding similarity between the original question and synthetic questions generated from the answer.
Microsoft's conversation-centric multi-agent framework; strong in enterprise/Azure ecosystems.
Synthesizing informal 'open codes' (first-pass error notes) into named failure-mode categories, typically LLM-assisted.
The algorithm that updates a neural network's weights by propagating the prediction error backward through the network layers.

cards.front: What is the 'Benevolent Dictator' eval process?
cards.back: One domain expert given authority to make judgment calls on error analysis, instead of routing every decision through committee.
Embeds query and document separately, then compares vectors — fast, used for initial retrieval at scale (as opposed to a cross-encoder).
A metric for evaluating generated text (especially translation) against reference text; higher is better.
A sparse/keyword-based retrieval algorithm; scores documents by term frequency, catching exact matches embeddings can blur together.

cards.front: What is a Business Associate Agreement (BAA)?
cards.back: A contract required under HIPAA before PHI can be sent to a third-party service. Attaches to a specific product surface, not a whole vendor — e.g. Azure OpenAI's BAA is automatic via Microsoft's licensing DPA, while AWS Bedrock/Vertex AI cover a model under the hyperscaler's own BAA.
When aggressive fine-tuning on a narrow dataset degrades a model's general capabilities outside that task.

cards.front: What is CBOW (Continuous Bag of Words)?
cards.back: A word2vec training method that predicts a target word from its surrounding context words.
Prompting the model to reason step-by-step before giving a final answer, improving accuracy on multi-step problems.
Splitting source documents into retrieval-sized units; strategies include fixed-size, semantic, hierarchical, and late chunking.
Any application can be both an MCP client and server simultaneously, enabling layered/hierarchical agent architectures.

cards.front: What is a Confusion Matrix used for in eval work?
cards.back: A breakdown of a classifier's (or LLM judge's) predictions by outcome type (true/false positive/negative) — reveals errors a single aggregate accuracy number hides.

The broader successor term to prompt engineering: deliberately designing everything that ends up in the model's context window — system prompt, retrieved chunks, tool definitions, memory, history — not just the instruction wording.

cards.front: What does RAGAS's Context Precision measure?
cards.back: Of the chunks retrieved, what fraction were actually relevant — signal-to-noise in retrieval.

cards.front: What does RAGAS's Context Recall measure?
cards.back: Of the chunks needed to answer a question, what fraction were actually retrieved — completeness of retrieval.
The maximum span of tokens a model can attend to in a single call; the model's 'working memory.'
RAG variant where the system evaluates retrieval quality before generating, triggering a fallback (reformulate + re-retrieve) if retrieved context is judged poor.
Standard measure of vector relatedness — the angle between two vectors, normalized to ignore magnitude.
In a decoder, an attention layer where Queries come from the decoder but Keys/Values come from the encoder — pulls information from the source input into generation.
Feeds query and document together into one model for a joint relevance score — slower but more accurate than a bi-encoder; used for reranking.

The requirement that data physically stay within a specific geography or infrastructure boundary. In regulated AI work this often picks the embedding model/vector store before quality benchmarks are even considered.
Python/pytest-native LLM eval framework; evals run as unit tests and fail CI on a metric threshold breach. 50+ built-in metrics including G-Eval.
Training a smaller, cheaper model to imitate a larger model's outputs on a specific task.
Trains a model on pairs of outputs (preferred vs. not) to directly optimize preference — simpler alternative to full RLHF.

The scaffolding code that runs a model/pipeline against a test set and scores results — not the metric itself, the thing that executes it repeatably. 'Harness Lib' (GitHub's code-completion eval system) is a named example: strip a function, regenerate it, re-run the original unit test.
A learned vector representation of a token, sentence, or document, positioned so semantically similar items are close together in vector space.
When an embedding model version changes, previously-indexed vectors are in a different semantic space than newly-embedded content — degrades retrieval silently if not re-indexed.

cards.front: What does RAGAS's Faithfulness metric measure?
cards.back: Whether every claim in a generated answer is actually supported by the retrieved context — decomposes the answer into claims and checks each against context.
Providing example input/output pairs in the prompt before the real request, most useful for unusual output formats.
Updating a model's weights (fully or via LoRA/QLoRA) on a specific dataset to change behavior (tone, format, task specialization) rather than knowledge.
A DeepEval metric using LLM chain-of-thought reasoning to score outputs against a custom natural-language rubric.

cards.front: What is a Golden Dataset / Ground Truth set?
cards.back: A labeled reference set of correct answers/outputs, curated by a domain expert, used to validate that an automated metric actually agrees with human judgment before trusting it at scale.
Retrieval over a knowledge graph of entities/relationships rather than (or alongside) vector similarity; suited to multi-hop reasoning questions.

Whether a model's output is tied to a specific, verifiable source rather than free-floating claims — the property faithfulness checking measures. 'Ungrounded' and 'unfaithful' describe the same failure from two angles.

Runtime checks that constrain model input/output to a safe or in-scope boundary — topic-scope enforcement, PII/PHI filtering, jailbreak detection. Guardrails AI and NeMo Guardrails are the two most commonly named implementations.
A model generating confident, fluent, but factually ungrounded or unsupported content.

cards.front: What is HNSW (Hierarchical Navigable Small World)?
cards.back: An approximate nearest-neighbor search algorithm using a multi-layer graph — the dominant indexing method for production vector search.
Combining sparse (BM25) and dense (embedding) retrieval to cover both exact-match and semantic-match failure modes.
Retrieval technique that embeds an LLM-generated hypothetical answer instead of the raw question, since a plausible answer is often closer in embedding space to real answer documents.
A model/training configuration value set before training (learning rate, batch size) rather than learned from data.
A vector index type that clusters vectors into buckets first — cheaper to build/update than HNSW, generally lower recall for the same speed.
Training technique that softens the target label (e.g. 1−ε instead of exactly 1) to reflect that language often has multiple valid continuations — improves metrics like BLEU.
Embedding a full document first (capturing document-level context), then splitting into chunks afterward, so each chunk's embedding retains full-document context.
Using an LLM to evaluate another LLM's output against defined criteria; should be binary (pass/fail) and validated against human labels via a confusion matrix.
Fine-tuning method that freezes original model weights and trains a small pair of low-rank matrices added on top — cheaper to train/store, swappable across tasks.

cards.front: What is the 'Lost in the Middle' phenomenon?
cards.back: LLMs reliably use information at the start/end of a long context but are measurably worse at using information buried in the middle.

Anthropic's open standard letting an LLM application connect to external tools/data sources through a common client-server interface instead of a custom integration per tool. A server exposes tools/resources; a client (agent host) consumes them.
Retrieval re-ranking that balances relevance against diversity, penalizing near-duplicate results.
Architecture routing each token to a small subset of specialized sub-networks, scaling total parameters without scaling per-token compute cost.
Answering a question that requires chaining multiple retrieval steps, where one retrieval's result informs the next query.
Generating several rephrased versions of a query, retrieving for each, then merging results to increase recall.
Writing an informal note describing the first specific thing wrong in a trace, before attempting to categorize it.
When a word/token at inference time wasn't seen during training and must be marked unknown; mitigated by subword tokenization.
Information encoded in a model's trained weights, as opposed to information supplied at inference time via context (retrieval).
A metric measuring how well a model predicts a sample of text; lower is better.

cards.front: What's the difference between PII and PHI?
cards.back: Personally Identifiable Information vs. Protected Health Information — overlapping but distinct. PHI is the HIPAA-specific subset where health context matters, not just the data itself: a name alone isn't PHI, a name tied to a diagnosis is.
Information added to token embeddings so a Transformer (which has no inherent sense of order via self-attention alone) can represent sequence position.
Marking a stable prefix of a prompt as reusable across calls so the model skips reprocessing it — cuts cost and latency.
Config-driven (YAML), language-agnostic LLM eval CLI; strong red-teaming/security-scanning engine (40+ attack types).
A training objective (like next-word prediction) used not for its own sake but because succeeding at it forces the model to learn a useful underlying representation.
LoRA plus quantizing the frozen base model to lower precision — further cuts memory requirements for fine-tuning on smaller hardware.
Compressing numeric precision (e.g. 32-bit floats to 8-bit or 4-bit) to reduce memory footprint and speed up computation, at some cost to precision.
Using an LLM to reformulate a user's raw query before retrieval (resolving ambiguity, adding synonyms, splitting compound questions).
RAG evaluation framework defining metrics including faithfulness, answer relevancy, context precision, and context recall.

Restricting who can invoke which capability based on assigned role rather than per-user rules. In an AI system, enforced at the retrieval/tool-execution layer — you can't filter sensitive content after it's already in the LLM's context.

cards.front: What is the ReAct (Reason + Act) pattern?
cards.back: Agent pattern alternating between generating a reasoning trace and taking a tool-call action, observing results, then reasoning again.
Deliberately attacking a model/system (prompt injection, jailbreaks, adversarial inputs) to find failure modes before a real attacker or user does.

cards.front: What is the Reflection agent pattern?
cards.back: An agent self-critiquing its own output against goal/criteria and iterating before finalizing.
Continuous evaluation against production traffic or a fixed dataset to catch silent quality drift after a model/prompt change.
A second, more expensive/accurate scoring pass (often a cross-encoder) applied only to the top-k candidates from initial retrieval.

cards.front: What is RLHF (Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback)?
cards.back: Training method using human preference labels to shape model behavior via reinforcement learning; limited because reward models can be gamed by adversarial inputs.
Method for merging ranked lists from multiple retrievers by summing 1/(k + rank) across lists, without needing to normalize disparate score scales.
An MCP server requesting an LLM completion from the client rather than needing its own model access — keeps servers lightweight.
Mechanism where every token computes a weighted relevance score against every other token in a sequence, letting representations be context-dependent.
An LLM parses a natural-language query into a structured metadata filter plus a semantic search query, applied together.
Splitting text at natural breakpoints (detected via embedding similarity between adjacent sentences) rather than fixed token counts.
A word2vec training method that predicts surrounding context words from a single target word (inverse of CBOW).
Embedding and searching at a small granularity for precision, then expanding to a larger surrounding window (parent chunk) at synthesis time.
Keyword/term-based retrieval (e.g. BM25); no semantic understanding, catches exact matches.
Constraining a model's response to a defined schema (e.g. JSON) rather than free text, for reliable downstream parsing.
Splitting text on word roots (bear/bears share a root) — the industry-standard tokenization approach, balancing OOV risk against sequence length.
Multi-agent orchestration where one central coordinator delegates tasks to specialist sub-agents and synthesizes their outputs.
If an agent reads sensitive data, it's flagged and prevented from writing to non-sensitive downstream locations.
The point in error analysis where you stop finding new categories of failure — signal to stop manually labeling traces.
The discrete unit (word, subword, or character) that text is split into before a model processes it.
The process of cutting text into tokens; approaches include word-level, subword, and character-level, each with different OOV/sequence-length tradeoffs.

cards.front: What is Tool Use / Function Calling?
cards.back: Giving a model structured definitions of available tools it can invoke, with the runtime executing the real function and returning results into context.
An LLM/RAG evaluation framework (alternative to RAGAS).
Testing a single LLM call/component in isolation before deployment, analogous to a software unit test.
The number of distinct tokens a tokenizer can produce; roughly tens of thousands for single-language models, hundreds of thousands for multilingual/code-capable models.
A 2013 technique for learning meaningful word embeddings via proxy tasks (CBOW, skip-gram); notable for capturing analogical relationships (king − man + woman ≈ queen).

An approval-gated arrangement where a vendor does not store inputs/outputs beyond what's needed for abuse prevention. Not default, and often mutually exclusive with other compliance modes (e.g. BAA 'Covered Models') — always verify which product surface an agreement covers.

A routing classifier placed before retrieval that picks the retrieval strategy (or skips retrieval entirely) per query based on its complexity. The formalized version of classic-RAG-vs-agentic-RAG routing.
Not a technique itself — a framing that treats every pipeline stage (indexing, retrieval, generation) as a swappable, independently-configurable module rather than a fixed sequence.

cards.front: How does Self-RAG differ from Corrective RAG (CRAG) or Agentic RAG?
cards.back: Self-RAG trains the decision to retrieve and the critique of its own output directly into the model's weights via reflection tokens. CRAG and Agentic RAG add that grading/retry logic as external orchestration around a model, not inside it.
